scope: Named r4.3 families and cited modeling extensions. A listed family can contain equivalent parameterizations. Assessment is per study and eligible profile.
premises: For T1 and T2, assume a single dose, zero initial amounts, central input and central concentration, and linear time-invariant one-compartment or reversible mammillary disposition. T1 additionally requires immediate non-increasing input. T2 requires a single log-concave input rate and valid within-animal observations. The upstream gates determine whether the data support a formal result.

piotrovskii1987: Cumulative human theophylline and rat pantothenic acid data illustrate an empirical distribution of absorption times.
savic2007: Savic et al. (2007), transit versus fixed lag
Four drug datasets provided a comparison of gradual transit with a fixed delay. The fitted result is specific to those datasets.
gabrielsson2016: Gabrielsson et al. (2016), Pattern Recognition in Pharmacokinetic Data Analysis

Cases 4–5 illustrate the value of IV data for disposition. In case 16, the finite zero-order fit described one volunteer’s oral profile better than the tested first-order fit with its own onset assumptions.
weiss1996: Extended-release oral and intravascular reference data were fitted together to estimate the distribution of input times.
kim2015: IV and oral peaks plus bile-related evidence supported a recycling model for fimasartan. A second group-mean peak alone cannot identify recycling in another drug.
levitt2003: Known simulated inputs illustrate how the IV reference, sampling and noise affect reconstruction.
larsen2015: Larsen et al. (2015), intestinal gabapentin uptake
The gabapentin experiments provide a separate example of transporter-mediated uptake.
celiprolol2009: Experimental study of celiprolol transport in mice
The mouse transporter experiments provide a way to distinguish intestinal transport effects using independent evidence.

candidates.label: First-order input from dosing
candidates.next_check: Compare early, peak and immediately post-peak residuals on the same observations, with matched disposition, error and BLQ treatment. Repeat after omitting a key peak sample.

candidates.label: First-order input after a fixed lag
candidates.next_check: Compare early, peak and immediately post-peak residuals on the same observations, with matched disposition, error and BLQ treatment. Repeat after omitting a key peak sample.

candidates.label: Finite zero-order input from dosing
candidates.next_check: Compare early, peak and immediately post-peak residuals on the same observations, with matched disposition, error and BLQ treatment. Repeat after omitting a key peak sample.

candidates.label: Finite zero-order input after a fixed lag
candidates.next_check: Compare early, peak and immediately post-peak residuals on the same observations, with matched disposition, error and BLQ treatment. Repeat after omitting a key peak sample.

candidates.label: Single Weibull, 0 < β < 1, no lag
candidates.next_check: The rate decreases from an integrable singularity. Cumulative input starts at zero. Compare with the corresponding first-order or transit curve using matched assumptions.

candidates.label: Single Weibull, 0 < β < 1, fixed positive lag
candidates.next_check: The rate decreases from an integrable singularity. Cumulative input starts at zero. Bound the delay using dose time and early serial draws. Compare with the corresponding first-order or transit curve using matched assumptions.

candidates.label: Single Weibull, β = 1, no lag
candidates.next_check: This is first-order input with kₐ = 1/τ. It is the same model in a different parameterization. Compare with the corresponding first-order or transit curve using matched assumptions.

candidates.label: Single Weibull, β = 1, fixed positive lag
candidates.next_check: This is first-order input with kₐ = 1/τ. It is the same model in a different parameterization. Bound the delay using dose time and early serial draws. Compare with the corresponding first-order or transit curve using matched assumptions.

candidates.label: Single Weibull, β > 1, no lag
candidates.next_check: The rate starts at zero, increases smoothly and then declines. Compare with the corresponding first-order or transit curve using matched assumptions.

candidates.label: Single Weibull, β > 1, fixed positive lag
candidates.next_check: The rate starts at zero, increases smoothly and then declines. Bound the delay using dose time and early serial draws. Compare with the corresponding first-order or transit curve using matched assumptions.

candidates.label: Serial first-order transit from dosing
candidates.next_check: Compare an initially increasing input from serial positive-rate stages, with or without a final first-order absorption step, against Weibull β > 1 and a fixed delay. Estimate mean transit time only if identifiable.

candidates.label: Serial first-order transit after a fixed lag
candidates.next_check: Compare an initially increasing input from serial positive-rate stages, with or without a final first-order absorption step, against Weibull β > 1 and a fixed delay. Estimate mean transit time only if identifiable.

candidates.label: Parallel immediate non-increasing inputs
candidates.next_check: Compare fast and slow nonnegative fractions released from dosing. Establish mixture shape separately before applying a peak guarantee.

candidates.label: Sequential, interrupted or independently delayed input components
candidates.next_check: Verify a within-animal second rise, then compare separated input pulses with a single gradual input under shared disposition.

candidates.label: Initial burst plus sustained release
candidates.next_check: Verify early and late samples in the same subjects and seek independent release data. A burst followed by release can also produce a shoulder.

candidates.label: Inverse Gaussian input
candidates.next_check: Compare as an empirical sensitivity model with IV-informed disposition and early sampling. The r4.3 T1/T2 classification has not been assigned to this family.

candidates.label: Slower or capacity-limited input with preserved systemic extent (2a)
candidates.next_check: Check whether peak exposure falls more than common-window exposure. Test unchanged extent with complete AUC/dose and supported common clearance.

candidates.label: Saturable uptake or incomplete absorption reducing F (2b)
candidates.next_check: Compare complete AUC/dose across doses with IV clearance over the same range. Investigate independent transporter or site-loss evidence.

candidates.label: Saturable intestinal efflux increasing F (2c)
candidates.next_check: Verify gut exposure, comparable doses and complete AUC/dose. Compare against first-pass metabolism and systemic nonlinear elimination.

candidates.label: Saturable presystemic extraction increasing F (2c)
candidates.next_check: Confirm the portal contribution and compare systemic IV clearance, metabolites or portal exposure at comparable doses.

candidates.label: Dissolution, solubility or formulation-limited release
candidates.next_check: Compare formulations, administered concentration and independent dissolution or precipitation measurements at a relevant site.

candidates.label: Delayed or interrupted gastric emptying
candidates.next_check: Confirm enteral delivery, meal timing and gastric emptying against individual trajectories.

candidates.label: Regional uptake or a limited intestinal absorption window
candidates.next_check: Review GI transit, regional delivery and incomplete recovery across formulations or sites.

candidates.label: SC or IM depot release, local perfusion or injection-site loss
candidates.next_check: Compare injection site, volume, formulation and local measurements with a comparable systemic IV reference.

candidates.label: Parallel pulmonary and swallowed enteral input
candidates.next_check: Confirm administration route, lung deposition and swallowed fraction. Match local and systemic measurements before partitioning input.

candidates.label: Enterohepatic recirculation
candidates.next_check: Compare individual EV and IV profiles with comparable dose, sampling and feeding, then seek bile or mass-balance evidence.

candidates.label: Flip-flop kinetics (absorption-limited terminal decline)
candidates.next_check: Compare EV and IV tail windows for sensitivity to the last sample, estimate disposition from comparable IV data and test slow input jointly.

candidates.label: Ongoing ordinary absorption during the sampled decline
candidates.next_check: Compare continuing input and completed input against shared IV disposition. A declining concentration still permits ongoing absorption.

candidates.label: Multicompartment disposition masked by slow input
candidates.next_check: Resolve early distribution and the terminal IV phase, then compare joint IV/EV models.

candidates.label: Saturable systemic elimination
candidates.next_check: Check exposure-matched IV dose series. Low-concentration terminal slopes may converge despite nonlinear clearance at higher concentrations.

candidates.label: Dose-, occasion- or state-dependent clearance
candidates.next_check: Compare IV clearance in each state and dose range. Complete EV AUC/dose identifies F/CL when disposition is linear.

candidates.label: Changes in distribution or concentration-dependent binding
candidates.next_check: Check paired free and total concentrations, time-matched matrix measurements and IV distribution.

candidates.label: Amplitude change through systemic availability (F)
candidates.next_check: Assess complete matched AUC and independently justify common clearance. Test whether a constant multiplier is compatible with aligned times.

candidates.label: Amplitude change through proportional scaling of CL and V
candidates.next_check: Compare IV profiles in both conditions. Co-scaling CL and V preserves their ratio and can mimic a change in F.

candidates.label: Change in absorption rate alone
candidates.next_check: Test complete dose-normalized AUC under common linear disposition, then compare models that change only input timing.

candidates.label: Combined changes in input, extent or disposition
candidates.next_check: Start with the simplest distinguishable contrasts and seek independent evidence for each component before fitting their combination.

candidates.label: Accumulation or time-dependent input or disposition
candidates.next_check: Check dose history, matched occasions and interval exposures against the single-dose superposition prediction.

candidates.label: Predose drug, endogenous signal or carryover
candidates.next_check: Verify predose material, assay specificity, prior doses and washout before interpreting onset.

candidates.label: Sampling, averaging, assay or timing explanation
candidates.next_check: Trace dose and draw times, BLQ/ULOQ limits, observation units and animal identities. Re-examine the pattern within verified individuals.

candidates.label: Parallel linear and saturable absorption
candidates.next_check: Compare parallel first-order and capacity-limited absorption with single linear or capacity-limited input across dose levels. Check identifiability against nonlinear clearance.

candidates.label: Parallel linear and saturable elimination
candidates.next_check: Test linear plus Michaelis–Menten clearance with IV data across concentrations before attributing nonlinear EV exposure to absorption.

candidates.label: Between-subject variation in lag or absorption rate
candidates.next_check: Check early serial samples and dose timing by individual. Vary lag or rate across subjects before interpreting a pooled shoulder or secondary rise.

candidates.label: Finite administration duration
candidates.next_check: Check start and stop times for dosing and the formulation before attributing the delay to biological absorption.

candidates.label: Parallel finite zero-order and first-order input from dosing
candidates.next_check: Test the fraction entering by each route under common disposition. The sum of these two immediate, non-increasing rates satisfies T1.

candidates.label: Dose-proportional exposure or concentration profiles
candidates.next_check: Review the separate T3 exposure and T3p concentration contrasts on their specified doses and windows.

candidates.label: Shared linear one-compartment EV/IV disposition
candidates.next_check: Inspect the matched ratio and T4 assumptions, including IV administration and the uncertainty model, before comparing alternative dispositions.
